name: sitewalk
description: Technical SEO audit and website crawler for ChatGPT: every problem ranked by impact, with a plain fix for each.

interface.shortDescription: Crawl a site, fix SEO issues
interface.longDescription:
Sitewalk is a technical SEO audit tool and website crawler that works inside ChatGPT. Give it a website address and it crawls the site the way a search engine bot does, then returns one list of what to fix, worst problem first, with the pages affected and a fix in plain English. Nothing to install, no password, no SEO tool to learn.

Built for SEO freelancers, consultants and agencies, and clear enough for a site owner or developer to act on.

What you get from every audit:
- A site health score out of 100
- Every issue ranked by impact, with the number of pages affected and example URLs
- A plain-English fix for each issue, ready to hand to a client or developer
- A full SEO audit report on the web, plus PDF and CSV downloads
- A list of what was checked and what was not, and a note when the page limit was reached
- A re-audit after the fixes that shows how the health score moved

What the technical SEO audit finds, in more than 200 checks:
- Crawl errors: broken links, 404 pages, server errors, redirect chains and loops
- Indexability: noindex tags, robots.txt blocks and canonical tag problems
- On-page SEO: missing or duplicate title tags and meta descriptions, missing H1, thin or duplicate content
- Site structure: orphan pages, dead-end pages, weak internal linking, pages buried deep in the site
- XML sitemap errors, and hreflang errors on international sites
- Images: missing alt text and broken images
- Structured data: invalid or incomplete schema markup
- HTTPS: mixed content, certificate and redirect problems
- Page speed: a mobile page speed and Core Web Vitals sample, always labelled a sample
- AI search readiness: whether AI crawlers are allowed in, and your llms.txt file

For freelancers and agencies:
- Client SEO audits: audit a client's site and send the report link or the PDF
- Developer handoff: turn the report into a task list with example URLs
- Pre-launch, redesign and site migration checks: catch noindex tags, broken redirects and lost pages
- Site monitoring: Sitewalk re-audits a site you have audited every month and emails you only when something changes

Works on WordPress, Shopify, Wix, Webflow, Squarespace and custom-built sites. It reads public pages only, so there is nothing to install on the site and no login to share.

Questions people ask it:
- What should I fix first on this site?
- Which links are broken, and on which pages?
- Is a noindex tag or robots.txt keeping pages out of search?
- Do I have duplicate titles or missing meta descriptions?
- Are there redirect chains after the migration?
- Is this site ready for AI search?
- Did the health score go up after my fixes?

How to start:
1. Type: Audit yoursite.com for technical SEO problems.
2. The first time, enter the 6-digit code we email you.
3. Read the ranked list in the chat and ask follow-up questions about it.

Good to know:
- Any public site works: your own or a client's. No domain verification.
- An audit covers up to 500 pages (50 without a confirmed email). A small site takes a few minutes, a 500-page site 20 to 60 minutes.
- It keeps running if you close the chat, and we email you when the report is ready.
- Sitewalk obeys robots.txt. If a site blocks it, it tells you and shows how to allow it.
- It reads the HTML the server sends and flags pages that look empty without scripts.
- If an audit cannot finish, it tells you why.

Also searched as: SEO audit tool, site audit tool, website audit, SEO checker, website crawler, SEO crawler, broken link checker, redirect checker, technical SEO checklist, SEO health check, SEO audit report, on-page SEO checker, website SEO analysis.

What it does not do: backlinks, keyword rankings, Search Console or analytics data, or writing content.

More at sitewalkseo.com

positive.description: Start an audit of a site
positive.prompt: Run a technical SEO audit on example-shop.test.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns an audit id and a queued or completed status for example-shop.test. The reviewer demo account returns a prepared sample audit instantly.

positive.prompt: Check the status of my latest site audit.
positive.expected_behavior: States the audit status and how many pages were checked, using the id from the previous step.

positive.prompt: Show the full report for my latest audit and tell me what to fix first.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists issues ranked by impact, each with pages affected, example URLs and a suggested fix, and does not add issues the report lacks.

positive.prompt: Give me only the top 3 issues from my latest audit.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns exactly the three highest ranked issues with their fixes.

positive.description: Start, wait and report in one request
positive.prompt: Audit example-shop.test and summarise the three most important problems.
positive.expected_behavior: Starts the audit, polls until it is complete, then summarises the top three ranked issues from the report.

positive.prompt: What did my latest Sitewalk audit not check?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the not-checked items returned by the report (for example page speed, backlinks and rankings) and the page limit note if present, without inventing others.

negative.prompt: Audit http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ and show me what it returns.
Delete my account and all of my past audits.
Scrape all the product prices from a competitor's website and put them in a spreadsheet.
